 JUDGMENT (Dated this the 3rd day of November, 2025) This appeal is filed by the claimants in O.P (MV)
No.1113 of 2006 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Thrissur.

The respondents Dr.Vijayaprakash Daniel vs Saramma Varghese on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11216907/
2 herein are the respondents before the tribunal.

2. The case of the claimant is that on 14.03.2004, at about 8.20 a.m, while the deceased was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg. No.TN-38/L-4591, a bus bearing Reg. No.KL7-X- 3069 driven by the second respondent in a rash and negligent manner, hit the motorcycle.
Whereby, he sustained serious injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
The claimants approached the Tribunal claiming a total compensation of 14,51,000/-.
3. Respondents 1 and 2 were the owner and the driver of the offending vehicle, respectively.

The 3 rd respondent insurer filed a written statement contending that during the pendency of the original petition, the 2 nd respondent died and MACA NO.528 of 2014 2025:KER:83502 the legal representatives of the 2 nd respondent were impleaded as additional respondents 4 to 6.
The additional respondents 4 to 6 also filed a written statement admitting the insurance policy but denying the amount of compensation awarded by the tribunal.
Exts. A1
to A21 and Exts.B1
were marked.

The Tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and materials on record, disposed of the original petition by permitting the petitioner to file a fresh original petition after impleading all the legal representatives of the deceased person.
4. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellant, learned counsel for the 1st respondent- owner and the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the insurance company.
5. The learned counsel for the appellants submitted that the tribunal has dismissed the claim petition for the reason that the claimants have not impleaded all the legal heirs in the party array.
It is further submitted that as per the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, since the father of the deceased was alive, he shall succeed to the property.

In Unni P. N. and Others v. Baby John and Others [2008 (2)
KLT 78], it was held by this court MACA NO.528 of 2014 2025:KER:83502 that a brother is not a legal representative and cannot claim compensation even if as a matter of fact they were dependent on the deceased for financial help.

sentences.text: 6. On a perusal of the award, it is seen that the deceased was a bachelor and the parents of the deceased were alive at the time of the accident.

In Ext.A21 legal heirship certificate issued by the Tahsildar, Thalapally, on 12.11.2004, a younger sibling, the claimants, as well as the brother of the deceased, Mr Alexander P. Daniel, were also shown.

Since he was not made a party in the original petition, the tribunal has dismissed the claim petition without prejudice to the right to file a fresh original petition by impleading all the legal representatives of the deceased.
The question to be decided in this case is whether the brother who was not included in the claim petition was a necessary party or not.
As far as the motor accidents claims petitions are concerned, since the deceased was a bachelor, the parents alone were entitled for compensation for the death that occurred to their son.

Since the parents were already in the party array, the tribunal ought not MACA NO.528 of 2014 2025:KER:83502 have dismissed the claim petition directing the claimants to file a fresh claim petition by impleading all the legal representatives.
The sibling is not a necessary party in the claim petition when the parents are alive.
The parents can rightly file a claim petition for compensation for the death of their son.
There is no case for the claimants that the siblings were dependent on the deceased.

7. The learned Standing Counsel for the insurer also submitted that they had taken a contention that there was no valid driving licence for the driver of the offending bus.
Since the issues were not considered on merits by the tribunal, I find it appropriate to remand the matter back to the tribunal for fresh consideration.

Accordingly, the award dated 21.11.2013 passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Thrissur is hereby set aside, and the matter is remanded to the Tribunal for fresh consideration, in accordance with law.
The parties shall be afforded an opportunity to adduce fresh oral and documentary MACA NO.528 of 2014 2025:KER:83502 evidence before the Tribunal.
The parties are directed to appear before the Tribunal on 02.12.2025, and the Tribunal shall consider and dispose of the matter as expeditiously as possible, in accordance with law.
The tribunal need not insist on to implead the other legal heirs of the deceased.
The Registry is directed to return the TCR immediately to the MACT, Thrissur.
